items.title: Marquee Setup for Windows
items.text: Setting Marquee up on Windows no longer needs a terminal. Marquee Setup (in the Start menu, or MarqueeSetup.exe from the release page) walks you through your library, network, sign-in, services and start at boot, and checks your keys and ports as you go.

items.title: Game clips as an add-on
items.text: Turn on Clipper on the Game clips page: Setup installs it on this PC, or gives you one command to paste on your gaming PC and shares the clips folder for you.

items.title: Marquee in lights
items.text: Marquee has a new icon when you add it to your phone's home screen: a lit-up marquee M. On Android it now fills the icon shape properly instead of sitting in a white circle. Already added Marquee? Remove it from your home screen and add it again to get the new icon (iPhones keep the old one until you do).

items.title: Take it with you
items.text: Going somewhere without Wi-Fi? Open a film or episode and press To phone (the phone button on episode rows). Marquee makes a small copy (Small 480p, about 450 MB an hour, or Standard 720p) that plays in your phone's own video player with subtitles built in. Or download the file at full quality.

items.title: A whole season
items.text: Season to phone makes every episode of the season you're looking at. They're listed under For your phone in the Library, each with its own Download button as it's ready. With notifications on, you hear when one is done.

items.title: Phone copies
items.text: Copies are made one at a time with the GPU when it has NVENC, kept in cache/travel for 7 days after their last download (TRAVEL_KEEP_DAYS) and capped at 50 GB (TRAVEL_MAX_GB). HDR is tone-mapped to SDR.

items.title: Scrubbing looks the part
items.text: The picture you see while hovering or dragging along the timeline now sits in a small velvet card with the time in marquee gold, and a little pointer shows exactly where you'll land. While a preview is still loading, the card keeps its size instead of jumping.

items.title: Thumbs up, thumbs down
items.text: Rate any film or show from its page. Everyone sees who liked something ("Liked by Anna and Ben"); a thumbs down stays private.

items.title: Popular on Marquee
items.text: A new row near the top of Discover shows what people here liked and watched lately.

items.title: Chat and reactions in Watch Together
items.text: Open Room while watching together to send emoji that float over the picture, or chat. Messages pop up over the video, even with the controls hidden.

items.title: Plan a watch party
items.text: Pick a time from a film's or episode's page (the people icon) and send the invite. Everyone gets a countdown, and playback starts by itself for whoever's in the room. Your parties wait in Library. The host can also start a running room with a short countdown.

items.title: Marquee Wrapped
items.text: Settings → Marquee Wrapped tells the story of your year: hours watched, top titles, your show of the year, your busiest days and who you watched with. It counts from today on.

items.title: Your own password
items.text: Marquee can now sign you in by itself. If the owner made you an account, you'll see a sign-in page when you're away from home, and Settings lets you change your password or sign out.

items.title: Safer from other websites
items.text: Marquee now ignores requests that other websites try to send through your browser, so a page you visit can't start downloads or delete anything.

items.title: Server security
items.text: Create sign-ins with node setup.js user add EMAIL. Visitors from the internet always sign in; HOME_NETWORK_ACCESS=signin makes people at home sign in too. On Windows, run node setup.js service install once in an admin PowerShell: it removes the old SYSTEM watchdog task. Clipper installs are now pinned and checksum-verified.

items.title: Hear when it's ready
items.text: Turn on notifications in Settings and your phone or computer tells you when a download is ready to watch, even with Marquee closed.

items.title: New episodes
items.text: When a new episode of a show you follow or have in your library arrives on Marquee, you'll get a heads-up. Each kind of notification can be switched off on its own.

items.title: Invite people to watch
items.text: In a Watch Together room, tap Invite and pick someone: they get a notification that opens the room.

items.title: On iPhone
items.text: Apple only allows notifications for apps on the Home Screen: tap Share, then Add to Home Screen, and turn notifications on from there.

items.title: Save for later
items.text: Press Save on any film or show to keep it in a Saved for later row at the top of Discover.

items.title: Download when it's out
items.text: Saved a film that isn't out yet? Tick "Download it when a good copy is out" and it downloads by itself once it's released, never a cinema recording.

items.title: Follow a show
items.text: Press Follow on a show and each new episode downloads by itself once it has aired. Episodes you already had aren't fetched again, and older episodes are left alone.

items.title: New and Coming up
items.text: Episodes that arrived this way show a New badge on the show until you open it, and the Library has a Coming up row with the next episodes and release dates.

items.title: Skip the opening titles
items.text: A Skip intro button now appears while a show's opening titles play (or press S). Marquee finds the theme song by comparing an episode with its neighbours, so it works even after a long cold open.

items.title: Or skip them automatically
items.text: Settings → Watching → Intros can skip openings on their own. Rewind into one and it plays as normal.

items.title: Night mode
items.text: Tap the moon in the player (or press N) to even out loud explosions and quiet dialogue, with voices lifted so you can keep the volume down.

items.title: Sleep timer
items.text: Also under the moon: pause after 15 minutes to an hour and a half, with the sound fading out gently, or at the end of the episode so the next one doesn't start while you sleep.

items.title: Subtitles your way
items.text: The subtitles menu now sets the style (a dark box, a soft shadow or an outline) and how high the lines sit, as well as the size.

items.title: Two languages at once
items.text: Pick a Second language in the subtitles menu to show it above the first. Handy for learning a language, or when you're watching with someone who reads another.

items.title: What's new, right here
items.text: From now on, Marquee shows you what changed after each update, just like this. You can read past updates any time in Settings → What's new.

items.title: Next episode starts with the credits
items.text: When the credits roll, an Up next card counts down and plays the next episode. Pause or tap Keep watching to stay where you are.

items.title: Stats for nerds
items.text: Press I while watching, or right-click the picture, to see everything about the stream: resolution, codecs, HDR, bitrate, dropped frames, buffer and download speed. Copy puts it all on your clipboard.

items.title: Previews while you seek
items.text: Drag along the timeline to see a small picture of that moment before you let go.

items.title: Subtitles that line up
items.text: Subtitles are checked against the audio and fixed when they drift, even when they were made for a different cut of the film.

items.title: Always up to date
items.text: Finished downloads, deletions and where you stopped watching on another device now show up straight away, without reloading.

items.title: Add to library
items.text: If someone else already has a title on the server, Download becomes Add to library: it's yours instantly, with nothing to wait for.

items.title: Exact clip cuts
items.text: Game clips can now be cut on any frame, not just the nearest keyframe, with no loss in quality.

title: Episode pictures and a tidier library

items.title: A picture for every episode
items.text: Episodes now show a still from the episode itself in the season list, Continue watching and Up next, so you can spot the one you want at a glance.

items.title: Delete a season or a whole show
items.text: A show's page can remove one season or the whole show in one go, instead of episode by episode.

items.title: Ready to play sooner
items.text: New downloads are prepared for playing about twice as fast, and Firefox gets its own copy straight away instead of when you press Play.

items.title: Tidier subtitles
items.text: Subtitle lines no longer crowd into each other, and long lines stop wrapping too early in Firefox.

items.title: Steadier TV casting
items.text: Play on TV keeps playing the file it started with, even if the library changes underneath it.

items.title: Notes on your phone
items.text: Notes fit small screens now: easy-to-tap actions with undo, the keyboard no longer covers what you're typing, and images open full screen.

items.title: Search inside images
items.text: Text in note images (screenshots, receipts, posters) is read automatically, so a search finds them too.

items.title: Notes and clips in Discord
items.text: A shared note shows as a preview card in Discord with its images or video. Shared clips open in Marquee's own player, at full quality.

items.title: Better clip editing
items.text: Cut several parts out of a clip in one edit, and leave out audio tracks you don't want, like a noisy mic.

items.title: House: Sharing and Screen Time
items.text: House → Sharing shows what streams and encodes cost the server right now. Screen Time shows how long each computer at home has been used, and on what.

items.title: Download in one press
items.text: Download picks the best release for you from your quality setting, size limit and audio language. For a show, choose the season and press Download Season.

items.title: Episodes in order
items.text: Episode one downloads first and at full speed, so you can start watching while the rest of the season finishes.

items.title: 1440p
items.text: Between 1080p and 4K, there's now a 1440p choice for sharp pictures without 4K's size.

items.title: One library
items.text: Downloads show on the title's own card in your library, episode by episode, as soon as each one is ready.

items.title: A library that keeps itself current
items.text: New downloads and changes appear in the library on their own, and when an episode ends, Marquee offers the next one.

items.title: Notes
items.text: A shared Notes tab for messages, links, photos and videos. Photos and videos uploaded from a phone stay private to Marquee.

items.title: Rename clips
items.text: Give a clip a proper name instead of the recorder's timestamp.

items.title: Your own account
items.text: Everyone signs in to their own Marquee: your library, where you stopped and your settings are yours. If someone else already has a title on the server, add it to your library instead of downloading it again.

items.title: Settings
items.text: A Settings tab for colour themes, default subtitles, preferred quality, the page Marquee opens on and how your library is sorted.

items.title: Watch Together
items.text: Start a room from the player and send the link: playback stays in sync for everyone, and each person picks their own subtitles. Links show a preview in Discord.

items.title: Shows by season
items.text: Shows appear once in your library with their seasons and episode names. When there's no good season download, Marquee gets it episode by episode.

items.title: Library clean-up
items.text: Videos leave your library 7 days after they finish downloading unless you tap Keep, so old downloads don't pile up on the server.

items.title: Arrows on Discover
items.text: Rows on Discover have arrows, so you can scroll them with a mouse.

items.title: House
items.text: The House tab shows the server's disks, downloads and services, plus the computers at home. Wake the gaming PC and pick Linux or Windows, or restart it into the other.

items.title: Clips
items.text: Game clips from the PC, grouped by game, with share links that play right inside Discord. Trim them without losing quality, or delete the ones you don't want.

items.title: Invite links
items.text: Make a one-time invite link in Activity: the person enters their email and gets access, no dashboard needed.

items.title: New player controls
items.text: A seek bar that shows how much has loaded and the time under your finger, volume that's remembered, and everything in one row. On phones, double-tap left or right to skip 10 seconds.

items.title: Subtitles that make room
items.text: Subtitles are sized to the picture and move just far enough to clear the controls while they show. On an upright phone they sit in the empty space below the picture.

items.title: Keyboard shortcuts
items.text: Space to pause, arrows to skip and change volume, F for fullscreen, C for subtitles and more. Press ? while watching to see them all.

items.title: Pause or remove downloads
items.text: Downloads can be paused, resumed or deleted from their card.

items.title: Plays in Firefox
items.text: Browsers that can't play HEVC video, like Firefox, get a copy they can play, made automatically.

items.title: Subtitles fix themselves
items.text: Subtitles are lined up with the audio automatically when they're out of sync.

items.title: Nudge subtitles
items.text: If a line still shows up early or late, shift the subtitles in small steps from the player.

items.title: Safari and iPhone
items.text: Videos now play in Safari on Mac, iPhone and iPad.

items.title: Theater mode
items.text: In theater mode the player bar hides itself and the video sits in the middle of the screen.

items.title: One remote
items.text: When you cast to a TV, the remote shows only on the device that started it.

items.title: Activity log
items.text: The owner can see what happened on the server: who watched, downloaded and deleted what.

items.title: AirPlay and Chromecast
items.text: Send a film or episode to your TV at full quality.

items.title: Home TVs stay at home
items.text: The TVs at home are only offered when you're on the home network.

items.title: Ready sooner
items.text: New downloads are picked up for playing every 30 seconds instead of every two minutes.

items.title: Welcome to Marquee
items.text: Find films and shows, download them to the server and stream them in your browser, on any device.
